question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered configuration layers and the RFC’s earliest-owner and monotonic-policy rules as a permanent supported core contract?
rationale: The proposal adds a new CLI/configuration mode and determines which managed configuration source controls security-sensitive values; implementation tests cannot decide whether those semantics are the product’s intended long-term authority model.

options.title: Approve synchronized V1
options.body: Accept the bounded startup-only contract after confirming that the RFC and linked implementation encode identical precedence and security semantics.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft and require targeted changes to conflict ownership or monotonic policy handling before accepting the direction.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Leave managed composition in hosting systems and close the RFC and linked implementation if OpenClaw should not own this contract.

recommendation.title: Approve synchronized V1
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded startup-only contract after confirming that the RFC and linked implementation encode identical precedence and security semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline routes the proposal to steipete, who is the strongest available product-direction owner for accepting a new core configuration contract.
